name: building-lifecycle
description: Building lifecycle: place, upgrade to T2, move, then demolish

steps.description: role: player (issue #515): building #1's Upgrade button is present and ENABLED — `upgradeBtn.disabled` (BuildMenu.ts) only checks `nextTier === null` or affordability, not the research lock. A real click intercepts client-side (`if (nextTier !== null && nextLocked) { this.setStatus(...); return; }`) and never even issues `build upgrade 1` — a stricter no-op than the console command's own rejection, but the same observable outcome (buildingCount unchanged). Not `guard`: the button is reachable, just ineffective while locked.

expect.note: rejected: Tier 2 management_office is not researched — confirms this is a genuine no-op, not a silent success

steps.description: role: bootstrap (issue #515): building #2 was never placed, so there is no row and no button in the DOM at all — not merely disabled. `expect.blocked` needs a present-but-unusable control (interaction-driver.ts's checkGoal refuses an absent selector: "not in the DOM, so blocked proves nothing"), which doesn't exist here, and no player can ever target an id that was never shown to them. Genuinely bootstrap: this exercises the console's own bad-id guard, not a control a player could reach either way.

expect.note: rejected: Building #2 not found — only building #1 was ever placed

steps.description: role: bootstrap (issue #515): same reasoning as the `build move 2` step above — building #2 was never placed, so there is no row and no button in the DOM to point `expect.blocked` at, and no player can ever target an id that was never shown to them.

expect.note: rejected: Building #2 not found — the real building #1 is still standing
